complexity.notes: Quadratic, and the inner range is deliberately not clamped to the end of the array: when i + nums[i] runs past the last index, range() still yields those indices, but dp[j] never sees them. dp[-1] is set True before the loop and never rewritten, so any() finds it and abandons the generator at the last index at the latest, before an out-of-range one is produced. That short-circuit is load-bearing rather than lucky: it is what keeps this from raising IndexError, and it is also what bounds each inner scan at min(nums[i], n - 1 - i) instead of nums[i], so the run stays O(n^2) however large the values grow. It does leave the reader to reconstruct the argument, where min(i + nums[i] + 1, len(nums)) would state it. An O(n) time, O(1) space single pass exists via ||tracking the farthest index reachable so far||, or equivalently scanning from the end for ||the leftmost position that can reach the end||.
complexity.summary: Bottom-up DP: dp[i] is True if any index reachable from i (within nums[i] jumps) can itself reach the end; fills the table right to left and returns dp[0].
